proposals.proposed_docstring:
Whether an existing workload policy requests CPU-work animation pacing.

Return False if the policy has not been created, is disabled, or does
not report CPU-heavy work. This query does not create the policy.
:meth:`AmbientWidget._follow_the_run` uses True to cap a qualifying
backdrop at no more than :data:`_RUN_FPS`, rather than to stop it.
That caller can also request the same cap independently through
:func:`spacr.qt.gil_priority.active`. The animation switch, visibility,
Reduce motion and minimization still decide whether the backdrop runs;
this flag does not inspect those conditions.

GPU-only work is handled separately by :func:`_decorative_gpu_blocked`
and the policy's Spaceout fractal holds, not by this CPU-work flag.

:returns: True only for an existing enabled policy with CPU work marked busy.

proposals.proposed_docstring:
Whether the enabled workload policy reports CPU-heavy work.

True means both :attr:`enabled` and :attr:`cpu_busy` are set. It is a
CPU-work policy flag, not a statement that every animation has stopped.
Backdrop callers use it to cap their configured rate at no more than
:data:`_RUN_FPS`; the policy also holds eligible Spaceout fractals.
GPU-only work does not set this flag. :meth:`blocks_gpu` reports the
separate decorative GPU restriction; the policy uses that decision
to hold eligible GPU-backed Spaceout fractals.

:returns: True only while this policy is enabled and CPU work is marked busy.

caller_evidence.fact: AmbientWidget._rate returns min(configured_fps,_RUN_FPS) only when run_paced; _RUN_FPS=30 at668 is a configured cap, not achieved motion.
_follow_the_run paces for gil_priority.active OR CPU-policy helper, so policy Off does not disable independent pipeline pacing.
_should_run tests animation switch/visibility/Reduce motion/minimized state; _sync_run_state follows rate before deciding start/stop. Helpers do not themselves inspect these guards.
pauses_animation returns enabled AND cpu_busy; blocks_gpu separately returns enabled AND(cpu_busy ORgpu_busy). GPU-only work therefore does not make CPU flagTrue.

Policyapply only calls _hold_fractals while blocks_gpuTrue; eligible unpaused live fractals held for CPU flag or GPU backend, tracked for release. Do not imply every animation or every fractal is always paused.
Policycreation requires QApplication. Wrapper reads _RESOURCE_POLICY directly and never creates it; False if absent.

Decorative engine refuses GPU during policy block; independent external-compute and backend checks also exist. CPU and GPU work both block decorative GPU; policyOff alone does not promise unrestricted rendering.
active means at least one worker responsiveness claim, independent of Dynamic animation switch.
Policy enabled initializes from saved preference; errors fallbackTrue; job resource classification feeds cached busyflags. No external CPU load monitor implied.
